title: Reality Check
summary: Repeated attempts with small data are more effective than one random viral moment.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Consistency wins — not just one hit.
- Many start enthusiastically and stop quickly — because they expect a big result from the first two videos.
- The rule: Useful repeated attempts are more important than a random success snapshot.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Few numbers at the start can be intimidating.
- In the beginning, the numbers are small — and this is very normal even for good accounts.
- What stops you is not the reality — but the interpretation of the numbers as a final judgment.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: Work with Small Experiments and Simple Data
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Instead of saying «the video failed» — ask: What did I learn from the first 5 seconds?
- Focus on easy indicators: completion rate, saves, direct messages, or meaningful comments — these are signals that the content is truly useful.
- Real progress shows when you repeat the attempt with the same idea and one adjustment each time — iteration.
- Your goal at this stage is to build a steady workflow — not to chase a big number quickly. Small data is enough for a simple decision.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Quick Judgment or Smart Testing?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Exhausting Approach | Practical Approach |
|----------------|----------------|
| «The video did not bring a big number — so the idea is dead» — you close the door before you learn | «I repeat the same idea from a different angle and measure the difference» — you build real knowledge about your audience |

sections.subtitle: 3 Measurement Keys
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Iteration | Re-executing the same idea with a specific adjustment to learn | Same topic — but a different hook |
| Signal | A small indication that the content is truly useful | Comment: «I tried it and it worked» |
| Small Data | Few data points — but enough to make a simple decision | Top 2 out of 5 ideas in terms of completion |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: You have two ideas: one is trending but has no clear problem — and the other has less search but solves a real pain for your audience. Which one do you choose for the first test?
The trend — because it guarantees higher views.
The idea that solves a real problem — even if the numbers are lower.
Leave both until new inspiration comes.
Explanation: In Reality Check, we build on real utility — because that gives you useful signals in the long run.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Review 5 Ideas and Identify the Real Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Choose 5 ideas from what you have in mind — evaluate each one quickly: does it solve a real problem for a clear audience? Submission: For each idea (1–5): the idea + the problem + yes/no · at the end: two ideas you will try this week and why. Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criterion |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Clarity of Problem | 60% | Each idea is linked to a clear problem for a specific audience |
| Practical Decision | 40% | Choosing two ideas to test with a clear reason |

sections.contentMarkdown:

- You can: with each attempt make your decisions faster and clearer.
